description: PRODUCTION deployment for the real test (real_signal/REAL_TEST_PLAN.md). certificate, password, signup_signed, signup_kyber and signup_one_time come from the registered account (lss-provision export-account ... deployment-hints.json). profile libsignal: the sessions run with SIGNAL_CLIENT_PROFILE=libsignal (signal-seal-official, bundle-seal 80c-1, the official request frames). handshake 1122: measured 2026-11-12 (real_signal/state/handshake-production.json): chat.signal.org sends EncryptedExtensions, Certificate (one Ed25519 certificate), CertificateVerify (Ed25519) and Finished coalesced in ONE encrypted record of 1122 bytes (16 bytes of record padding); a new server certificate of another length changes it. signup_ciphertext 240 is Signal-Android's first text with a 108-character token (seen in the first real run, 2026-11-12: receive-session 134 2027 0 2 4 4 1 1 240 1 1 0), 176 the test sender's legacy layout; signup_hints 0 and 1. CONTACTS WITH LINKED DEVICES (2026-11-12: the first real run's contact has three devices; our reply was answered 409 and the refresh was refused at bundle-shape 8192): devices 4 (the server allows six; five need record class 14336, whose opening kernel does not lower in reach of this machine: tls-open-typed 12288 already peaks at 23.6 GB, so produce with --max-gb 26; a fifth device's response is refused in strict mode and the contact's message reported failed; a sixth device would not fit one request record anyway);bundle_slots 1: bundle-slot reads a device's item whatever the digit counts of its numbers (TlsMpc/BundleSlotKernels.lean; bundle_items, one kernel per digit-count combination, would need about 11,500 kernels for realistic ranges); device_lists pending: after a refresh every device is one that has not answered, so the request frames are 2^n per message class for n devices, not 3^n; record_max 12288: the prekey response of four devices is a record of up to 10,419 bytes (three: 7,861; the real run's three devices: 7,843; five: 12,976, not covered); scan_record_max 10240: above it only tls-open-typed and tls-reveal-masked are listed (the framing-scan kernels of 12288 do not lower under any cap this machine allows, and run only on small handshake records). A record above 12288 (five or more devices, or four or more queued deliveries packed in one record) is refused in strict mode. signup_jump 3 (the sessions run with SIGNAL_RECEIVE_JUMP=3, run_real_test.py sets it): a phone whose earlier signup we never answered (the first real run's contact was lost with that run's in-memory database nodes) sends its next token as message number 1 of the same unanswered session; receive-session ... 3 accepts numbers 0 to 3, privately.
